text: Dying Rachel named her son Ben-Oni, "son of my sorrow." His father renamed him Benjamin, "son of my right hand."
explanation:
When Rachel gave birth to Joseph, she named him in faith: "The Lord shall add to me another son." Years later, as she died giving birth to that second son, she called him Ben-Oni, son of my sorrow. "But his father called him Benjamin": son of my right hand, the place of power, favour and blessing.

It's a picture of a generation God is raising up in these last days, a grace generation. Some will try to load it with guilt: "Your mother died because of you; grace is ruining the church." But it's the Father who names this generation, not the critics. You're not a child of sorrow. You're a son or daughter of His right hand.

text: Benjamin received five times as much food as his brothers, and five changes of clothing. Five is the number of grace.
explanation:
When Joseph finally saw Benjamin, his only full brother, he had to leave the room to weep. His first words to him were, "God be gracious to you, my son." At the meal, "Benjamin's serving was five times as much as any of theirs." Later Joseph gave each brother a change of clothes, "but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments."

Jesus said not to worry about what you'll eat or wear, and here is a generation lavishly supplied with both. Five recurs throughout Scripture as a number of grace. Five changes of garments may also picture a manifold grace: an anointing that can flow in more than one way. Grace doesn't ration.

text: Zechariah couldn't speak until he wrote, "His name is John": Yohanan, "the Lord is gracious."
explanation:
When Gabriel announced that Zechariah's elderly wife would bear a son named John, the old priest didn't believe it, and he was struck mute until the promise was fulfilled. Nine months later, relatives wanted to name the baby after his father. Zechariah asked for a tablet and wrote, "His name is John." Immediately his mouth was opened, and he began to praise God and prophesy.

John, Yohanan, means "the Lord is gracious." Those who don't believe the message of grace often find they have nothing to say; the passion to share dries up. But the moment you write "grace" over your life, your mouth is loosed again.

text: At the well, she called Him "a Jew," then "Sir," then "a prophet," then "the Christ," and then she became an evangelist.
explanation:
Nicodemus, a learned teacher of Israel, came slowly to faith; only after the cross did he openly honour Jesus. But the Samaritan woman, living with a man who wasn't her husband after five marriages, grew in revelation within hours. "How is it that You, being a Jew…?" "Sir, You have nothing to draw with." "Sir, I perceive that You are a prophet." Then Jesus said, "I who speak to you am He."

She left her waterpot and ran into the town: "Come, see a Man who told me all things that I ever did. Could this be the Christ?" Many believed because of her. It was to her, not the theologian, that Jesus revealed true worship. Grace can transform people faster than anyone imagines.

text: At the cross, John was the one disciple still there. He called himself "the disciple whom Jesus loved."
explanation:
When Jesus hung on the cross and needed someone to care for His mother, all the other disciples had fled. John was there. "Woman, behold your son!… Behold your mother!" Yet John never called himself "the disciple who loved Jesus." He was conscious of Jesus' love for him, not his love for Jesus.

That's the secret. Those most conscious of receiving His love end up serving Him most, often without realising they're serving at all. You don't come to Jesus mainly to learn how to serve Him harder. You come to learn how to receive, and out of that, service flows.

text: As Joseph sent his brothers home, he said, "See that you do not quarrel along the way."
explanation:
Joseph had just revealed himself, forgiven them and loaded them with provisions. Then, as they set out, he added a very human word of advice. He knew what would happen otherwise: "It was your idea to sell him!" "No, it was yours!" "I wasn't even there!"

It's a word for us too, as we journey home toward the One who forgave us. Don't fight about whose fault the past was. Don't turn on each other along the way. Think about His glory, carry His provision, and love one another as He has loved you.

text: "He who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit." Law persecutes grace, never the reverse.
explanation:
Paul says Hagar and Sarah represent two covenants: Hagar is Mount Sinai, "which gives birth to bondage," and Sarah is the Jerusalem above, which is free. Both sons had the same father, Abraham. "But, as he who was born according to the flesh then persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, even so it is now."

It's always the son of the law who persecutes the son of grace. Many who criticise grace have the same heavenly Father as you, but not the same mother. And notice Paul's conclusion: "Cast out the bondwoman and her son." Sarah doesn't need Hagar's help to raise Isaac. Grace doesn't need the law brought back to keep you holy.
